description.narrative: The Project is expected to have the following Development Impact: (a) Stakeholders effect Increased Availability of Climate Finance: IFC will provide up to 5 years financing that will be leveraged by the Bank to grow its green portfolio which requires availability of longer-term capital. This will help in improving access to climate finance, contributing to the overall reduction in GHG emissions. IFC estimates that this investment will result in greenhouse gas reduction of approximately 31,376 tCO2e by 2027. As a reporting indicator, IFC will track the green-house gas emission reduction per year; and (b) Contribution to Market Creation - Sustainability: IFC anticipates that the Project will promote sustainability through the issuance of the first green bond in the country that will set standards for further such issuances and increase overall climate/green financing in Jordan. The Project is expected to establish and set the standards for green bonds in the market and hence encourage replication by other issuers. This is expected to mobilize incremental long-term resources for climate finance related projects and raise awareness among private sector companies of the merits of diversifying their financing sources and attracting capital markets financing to support green projects. As the first green bond in Jordan, the Project will set standards for the future issuances and introduce a new asset class to the local capital markets, which is expected to generate strong interest and pave the way for climate capital market transactions for a wide array of investors.

The proposed investment is for IFC to subscribe to up to US$ 50 Million in the first green bond to be issued by Jordan Kuwait Bank (the Bank or JKB) in Jordan covering the full issuance and up to US$ 40 Million GTFP trade line for up to one year (the Project). The investment will include an up to US$ 36 million investment from IFCs own account and up to US$14 million co-investment through IFC Blended Finance participation by Canada-IFC Blended Climate Finance Program (BCFP) and MENA Private Sector Development (PSD) facilities as described in the Blended Finance Section. The bond proceeds will be used by the Bank to finance eligible green projects and assets in Jordan.
